messages:
olivia: Quick question — my partner's child (turned 22) will be studying in the US on an F-1 this summer. Open enrollment just closed. Can I add them mid-year to my medical/dental/vision? No SSN yet.

people-ops: Hi @olivia — stepchildren are eligible up to age 26. Mid-year additions require a qualifying life event (QLE) or an eligibility exception like a recent move to the US or new full-time student status.

olivia: They just started full-time classes in the US this month. Is that a QLE? What docs do you need?

jamal: Gaining full-time student status can count as a QLE if it’s a change in eligibility. Docs we accept: passport + visa (I-20), current university enrollment letter, birth certificate or other proof of relationship, and if custody is informal then a notarized statement from the custodial parent. If no SSN, we use SSN=TBD and you update later.

benefits-bot: Secure upload: https://benefits.redwood.com/upload — choose category "dependent_enrollment" and include brief notes: "summer student QLE + move date". Allowed: pdf, jpg, png.

hr-intake: Filename convention: lastname_firstname_doc_YYYYMMDD.pdf (example: park_lee_i20_20260601.pdf). Include move/enrollment dates in the upload notes.

olivia: Great — I have I-20, enrollment letter, passport scans, and a notarized statement from the custodial parent. Uploading now and will add the move date (05/15/2026).

people-ops: Perfect. Once received we'll route to the carrier. If carrier accepts QLE, coverage can be effective retroactive to the event date; otherwise it will wait until next open enrollment. Payroll changes usually apply the first full pay cycle after carrier confirmation (1-2 pay periods). We'll tag payroll when confirmed.

benefits-bot: Upload received: park_lee_i20_20260515.pdf. Intake ticket #B-2026-789 created. Estimated review 1-3 business days. We'll update this thread when the carrier responds. :white_check_mark:
